data.title: Elastic Security Achieves the Only Perfect Score in the 2026 AV-Comparatives Endpoint Prevention and Response Test
data.description:
Elastic (NYSE: ESTC) today announced that Elastic Security achieved the only perfect protection score in AV-Comparatives' 2026 Endpoint Prevention and Response (EPR) Test, earning Certified Leader status, the highest distinction AV-Comparatives awards in the test. Elastic sits at the very top of this year’s Certified Leader group, with 100% Active and 100% Passive Response scores and the lowest modeled operational footprint of any product tested. This is the second consecutive year Elastic has earned Certified Leader status.

Elastic was the only vendor to block and report all 50 threats at the first phase of the test, before any progressed to Internal Propagation or Asset Breach. Elastic also had one of the lowest total costs of ownership (TCO) among the 14 vendors tested.

Prevention strength matters because AI-powered attacks no longer move at human speed. Adversaries now deploy automated toolchains that compress the time from initial access to lateral movement, data exfiltration, and persistence to minutes, not hours. At that velocity, detection and response alone cannot keep pace; the window to intervene after an intrusion begins is too narrow. Elastic stops more threats before they execute, matching machine-speed attacks with machine-speed prevention.

AV-Comparatives tested 14 vendors against 50 multi-phase attack scenarios built on techniques from the MITRE ATT&CK framework. Phase one covers the first three MITRE ATT&CK chain tactics: Initial Access, Execution, and Persistence. The scenarios included executables, scripts, Office add-ins, USB-propagated payloads, fileless execution techniques, AMSI bypasses, and EDR unhooking. This year’s test also incorporated AI-assisted development methods to build testing tools and scenario variations to better reflect how attacker tooling has evolved.

"Elastic Security achieved Certified Leader status in the AV-Comparatives EPR Test 2026,” said Andreas Clementi, Founder and CEO of AV-Comparatives. “The product prevented and detected every one of the tested attack scenarios already at the first stage of compromise with no operational accuracy costs and no workflow delays for the user. It is a clean, complete result that reflects real strength in enterprise threat prevention.”

“AI is compressing attack timelines, and security teams can’t afford more alerts to triage. They need to stop threats before they turn into investigations," said Mike Nichols, general manager, Security, Elastic. "Stopping every attack at the first phase of this test shows the strength of prevention in Elastic Security. A threat stopped at the endpoint is an alert that never opens, an investigation that never starts, and an incident that never escalates."

This result extends Elastic Security’s strong performance across recent AV-Comparatives testing. Across the last three Business Security Tests spanning 2025 and 2026, Elastic was the only vendor to achieve 100% malware protection in every cycle, including the most recent test covering March through June 2026, where Microsoft and CrowdStrike were among vendors tested.

Elastic Defend, Elastic’s native endpoint protection, is available for Windows, macOS, and Linux across cloud, on-premise, hybrid, and air-gapped environments.

Learn more about Elastic Security at elastic.co/security

Additional Materials

  • Blog: The only perfect Endpoint Prevention and Response (EPR) score in 2026 belongs to Elastic

data.title: EQ's Concentra awards $150,000 to credit unions strengthening Canadian communities
data.description:
Empowering Your Community program has awarded more than $2.3 million to credit unions making an impact, since its inception in 2011

TORONTO, Sept. 15, 2026 /CNW/ -- Equitable Bank (EQ) today announced that its subsidiary Concentra has awarded $150,000 to six credit unions through its 2026 Empowering Your Community (EYC) program. A leading partner to the credit union system, Concentra provides trust and financial service solutions to Canadian credit unions and has awarded more than $2.3 million to credit unions and their partners since the program's inception in 2011.

The grants come as Canadians increasingly look to institutions that strengthen their local economies. Member-owned and accountable to the communities they serve, credit unions turn local knowledge into local investment and are among the country's leading small-business lenders. EQ and Concentra are proud to stand with credit unions, supporting them in serving six million credit union members across Canada.

Since 2011, the EYC program has provided grants to credit unions across Canada in support of community causes that improve mental health, advance Indigenous resurgence, provide housing, and strengthen food security, putting capital directly behind the community organizations credit unions choose to stand beside. EQ is proud to continue engaging with credit unions and their partners as they create meaningful change in communities across the country.

"Credit unions play a unique role in Canada's financial ecosystem," said Tanya Postlewaite, Vice President, Trust and Credit Union Services at EQ. "Their deep community roots allow them to address local needs in ways few others can. This year's recipients reflect that strength, and through Concentra, we are proud to support their work in building more resilient and inclusive communities across Canada."

Winners of the 2026 Empowering Your Community grant include:

  • Access Credit Union and Assiniboine Credit Union – Awarded $100,000 to scale the Harvest Manitoba program in Winnipeg. Harvest Manitoba is a not-for-profit organization dedicated to reducing food insecurity across the province by collecting and distributing food, providing client-centered solutions, and advocating for long-term change. As Manitoba's provincial food network, Harvest supports more than 380 food banks and community agencies, working toward a future where no Manitoban goes hungry.

Additionally, $10,000 was awarded to each of the following credit unions for meaningful community initiatives:

  • Compass Credit Union and Rolling River First Nation (MB) for the MUSKODAA PISIKI (Buffalo) Project 
  • Alterna Savings and Credit Union Limited (ON) for Growing Resilience: Strengthening Ward 13's Community Food System Project 
  • Salmon Arm Savings and Credit Union (BC) for the Shuswap Community Teaching Garden Greenhouse Project 
  • Affinity Credit Union (SK) for the nēhiyawak Language Experience  
  • StellerVista Credit Union (BC) for the Full Bellies Full Hearts Project with Fernie Food Security Society

EQ and Concentra congratulate all 2026 grant winners and thank every credit union that applied. Together these initiatives show what the credit union system contributes to Canada: local decisions, local ownership and local results, at a time when the country is investing in its own capacity to grow. EQ and Concentra are proud to stand behind them.

About Equitable Bank

EQB Inc. () is a leading Canadian financial services company with approximately $151 billion in combined assets under management and administration. It is the parent company of Equitable Bank, the country's seventh largest Schedule I bank by assets, which operates EQ Bank, Canada's Challenger Bank™.

Our purpose is to remake banking so every Canadian gets ahead, every day. Since 1970, we have built thoughtful financial solutions that serve more than 4 million customers, turning everyday moments into meaningful progress. As the exclusive financial partner of Loblaw Companies Limited's PC Optimum™ loyalty program – one of Canada's largest loyalty programs with more than 18 million members – EQ Bank's financial solutions are deeply embedded into the daily lives of Canadians.

We provide personal and commercial banking services to Canadian households and businesses through everyday banking, tailored lending and connected payments, while fueling competition and choice in Canadian banking. Through our subsidiaries, we also offer home and auto insurance, estate and trust services, credit union solutions and alternative asset management.

To learn more, visit eqb.investorroom.com and eqbank.ca, or connect with us on Instagram, Facebook or LinkedIn.

data.title: Treasury Yields Edge Higher on Soft Demand at 20-year Auction — Market Talk
data.description:
1430 ET - Treasury yields tick higher as investors demand steeper returns to lend money to Washington long-term. A 20-year Treasury bond auction clears at a yield of 5.42%, the highest since 1986, when the tenor was discontinued, and since it was reintroduced in 2020. Still, demand indicators were on the soft side: the 2.57 bid-to-cover ratio was below the previous six-month average of 2.65, while indirect bidders, a group that includes foreign investors, took 52.5% of the bonds, also below average. The 20-year trades at 5.414%, up from 5.401% before the auction, while the 10-year rises to 5.014% from 4.996%. (paulo.trevisani@wsj.com; @ptrevisani)

1429 ET - Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent says he will meet with China's Vice Premier He Lifeng this weekend to continue discussing sanctions on Iran. "We have sanctioned three banks with China," Bessent says. "We have had some very good private discussions, and I look forward to those continuing this weekend when I meet my Chinese counterpart," he tells the House Financial Services Committee during a hearing. (jessica.coacci@wsj.com)

1311 ET - Rising bond yields beat out the prospect of an AI bubble as the biggest "tail risk," according to the latest Bank of America survey of global fund managers. About one-third of survey respondents named a "disorderly rise in bond yields" as the biggest tail risk, while 28% named an AI bubble, down from 32% in August. Bond yields have been climbing, fueled by surging energy prices brought on by the Iran war and growing national debt among other factors. The 10-year Treasury yield touched 5.04% earlier, its highest level since 2007. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1310 ET - The AI data center boom is expected to keep chugging along, according to Bank of America's latest survey of global fund managers. Of those surveyed, 79% said they do not expect one of the AI hyperscalers to announce a cut in capital expenditures this year, up from 71% in August. But investors see the spending as carrying some risk: 42% of respondents named AI hyperscaler capex as the most likely source of a systemic credit event, and net 33% said companies are overinvesting. As for the most crowded trade, 53% identified "long global semiconductors" which matched last month's survey. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1203 ET - Investors are increasingly expecting global interest rates to rise, according to findings from Bank of America's September survey of global fund managers. 41% of surveyed investors said they expect the Federal Reserve to raise rates before the U.S. midterms, up from 22% in August, while the proportion of investors who don't expect a rate hike fell to 52% from 72%. A net 32% of investors expect higher short-term rates, and net 25% said global monetary policy is too stimulative - with both metrics at their highest level since September 2022. Net 4% of investors expect lower global inflation, a reversal from the previous month. (elias.schisgall@wsj.com)

1133 ET - Bitcoin's price is under pressure from both long-term investors and short-term traders rushing to sell and lock in their profits, analysts with Glassnode say in a note. The cryptocurrency has bounced up to trade near a 47% premium to the average price that traders paid for it, meaning most sales are profitable right now, the analysts say. Long-term and short-term holders seem to be cashing out in roughly equal amounts, they say. But the shift toward profit-taking matches behavior seen during other price surges in recent years, signaling that the latest rally hasn't peaked or collapsed yet, the analysts say. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1110 ET - The Iran war is creating sharply different fiscal outcomes across the Gulf depending on countries' ability to keep hydrocarbons flowing, Capital Economics says. Higher energy prices are more than offsetting limited export disruption in the U.A.E. and Oman, improving their budget balances this year. By contrast, budget balances are expected to deteriorate by around 2% of GDP in Saudi Arabia, around 5% in Kuwait and Bahrain, and as much as 10% in Qatar compared with last year. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)

1059 ET - Bitcoin's recent pullback from the $79,000 level reflects continued uncertainty among investors ahead of the upcoming Federal Reserve meeting rather than a bearish trend reversal, XS.com's Simon-Peter Massabni says in a note. The cryptocurrency's price action of late highlights a clash between buyers trying to defend current levels and sellers concerned by a stronger U.S. dollar and rising interest rate expectations, Massabni says. "The Federal Reserve remains the most influential factor in Bitcoin's short-term outlook," he says. The central bank's interest rate decision is important, but so is the messaging that policymakers are sending about the future of monetary policy, Massabni says. Bitcoin is down 3% at $75,940, according to data from CoinGlass. (dean.seal@wsj.com)

1049 ET - Investors should focus on the vote split at the Bank of England rate decision on Thursday for a signal on the possibility of a BOE interest-rate increases in future months, Peel Hunt's Kallum Pickering says in a note. Additionally, communication by monetary policy committee members could provide clues, he says. If BOE Governor Andrew Bailey doubles down on his comments about second-round inflation effects being subdued, this could lower expectations of BOE rate increases, Pickering says. However, if the governor indicates higher inflation expectations then markets will see that as an endorsement of current market pricing, he says. Investors fully price in a total of four BOE rate increases by mid-2027, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

1006 ET - San Antonio is the most popular migration destination for Gen Zers, Redfin says. Houston is the hottest spot for millennial movers. Gen Zers are gravitating toward Washington, D.C. and Nashville--metros with plenty of job opportunities, along with lively social scenes. Millennials favor metro areas like Dallas and Baltimore--places that can offer more affordable housing. One thing the generations have in common: New York and Los Angeles are among the places they're most commonly leaving. Affordability is part of the story in pricey New York and Los Angeles, but Gen Z migration isn't purely about housing costs. Moves among young adults are also heavily influenced by college, first jobs and the transition from school into the workforce. (chris.wack@wsj.com)

1006 ET - The dollar could suffer some knee-jerk weakness if the Federal Reserve raises interest rates as expected but signals fewer future rate rises than markets anticipate Wednesday, TD Securities strategists say in a note. The Fed could lift rates by 25 basis points but this is largely priced in, they say. Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh could cite higher-than-expected inflation as the motivation for potentially raising rates, they say. While he'll probably avoid forward guidance, the dot plot projections could show a median of two rate rises, they say. The DXY dollar index rises 0.2% to 99.566. (renae.dyer@wsj.com)

1002 ET - Investors would increase their government bond allocations if yields climbed to an attractive level, such as the 30-year U.S. Treasury yield reaching 6%, according to 27% of fund managers in the Bank of America global fund manager survey for September. A total of 19% of fund managers polled said they would need to see "a major top in stock markets" before shifting their allocations towards more government bonds, the survey shows. U.S. 30-year Treasurys climbs 3.9 basis points to last trade at 5.367%, having hit a 19-year high of 5.401% earlier in the session, LSEG data show. (miriam.mukuru@wsj.com)

data.title: Wall Street dips as oil spikes and benchmark Treasury yields breach 5%
data.description:
Key points:
  • Indexes down: Dow 0.82%, S&P 0.47%, Nasdaq 0.78%
  • Traders price in 92% chance of Fed rate hike on Wednesday
  • Dave & Buster's slides after Q2 revenue miss
  • Crypto firms sink on bitcoin weakness

By Stephen Culp and Tharuniyaa Lakshmi

Wall Street extended its slide on Tuesday, as rising U.S. Treasury yields, mounting debt concerns and soaring crude prices kept buyers on the sidelines.

All three major U.S. stock indexes were lower in a broad selloff that weighed on nearly every sector but energy . That sector benefited from expanding hostilities in the Middle East, which included new attacks on Saudi Arabia's energy infrastructure.

"It is kind of a quiet market, but then you look at the advance/decline line, at the number of stocks that are moving in one direction, it is demonstratively to the downside over the last probably two weeks," said Paul Nolte, senior wealth adviser and market strategist at Murphy & Sylvest in Elmhurst, Illinois.

The Federal Reserve has convened for its two-day monetary policy meeting, which is due to culminate on Wednesday with the central bank's rate decision. With recent economic data showing the labor market on solid footing, while war-related energy price pressures are morphing into broader, systemic inflation, the central bank is expected to implement a 25-basis-point increase to its Fed funds target rate — its first interest rate hike in over three years.

In the wake of last week's hot inflation data and the near 25% jump in U.S. crude prices over the last two weeks, financial markets have priced in a near-certain 92.3% likelihood of a rate hike on Wednesday, up from 33.1% one month ago, according to CME's FedWatch tool.

"This will probably be not a one-and-done, but a series of rate increases," Nolte said. "It will be dependent on oil; that is really the source of inflation and it's starting to seep into other parts of the market."

As rate-hike bets increase, global bond yields resumed their upward climb, with benchmark U.S. Treasury yields breaching the 5% mark for the first time since 2007.

Rising interest rates are increasing the pressure on heavily indebted borrowers, including companies that have placed big bets on AI.

Those worries exacerbated mounting fears over AI's destructive potential and growing opposition to the construction of data centers, which came to a head on Monday and dragged the Philadelphia SE Semiconductor index 5.9% lower.

The semiconductor index, which has helped drive broader stock market gains this year, failed to meaningfully recover from Monday's rout, eking out a 0.3% gain.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 429.96 points, or 0.82%, to 51,991.24, the S&P 500 lost 36.03 points, or 0.47%, to 7,583.95 and the Nasdaq Composite lost 204.17 points, or 0.78%, to 25,982.25.

Among the 11 major sectors of the S&P 500, consumer discretionary stocks were the biggest percentage losers, while energy, buoyed by rising crude, advanced 2.3%.

Dave & Buster's tumbled 19.6% following the company's second-quarter revenue miss.

Waystar rose 7.3% after Reuters reported the healthcare software firm is exploring options, including a potential sale.

Weakness in bitcoin weighed down crypto firms Coinbase and Strategy 6.9% and 3.5%, respectively.

Declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.47-to-1 ratio on the NYSE. There were 97 new highs and 539 new lows on the NYSE.

On the Nasdaq, 1,413 stocks rose and 3,281 fell as declining issues outnumbered advancers by a 2.32-to-1 ratio.

The S&P 500 posted 12 new 52-week highs and 15 new lows while the Nasdaq Composite recorded 40 new highs and 239 new lows.

data.title: Dollarama 2Q Profit, Revenue Seen Higher as Value-Seeking Trend Continues — Earnings Preview
data.description:
By Adriano Marchese

Canadian dollar-store operator Dollarama is scheduled to report its fiscal second-quarter earnings Wednesday morning. Here's what you need to know.

REVENUE: According to FactSet, analysts expect revenue to rise to 2.02 billion Canadian dollars (US$1.45 billion) from C$1.72 billion a year earlier.

EARNINGS PER SHARE: Earnings are expected to rise to C$1.26 a share, compared with C$1.16 a year earlier.

ADJUSTED EARNINGS BEFORE INTEREST, TAXES, DEPRECIATION AND AMORTIZATION: Adjusted Ebitda is expected to rise to C$639.8 million, from C$588.5 million.

During the quarter, the stock rose 12% and recently traded at C$164.57.

WHAT TO WATCH

  • Dollarama has been a beneficiary of the consumer trend towards value, as a higher cost of living, rising inflation and interest rates put pressure on family budges. Investors will be keen to know the health of the Canadian shopper, and how the trend has continued to develop in the second quarter. RBC analyst Irene Nattel thinks that the trend is here to stay. "With household budgets pressured by elevated shelter costs, cumulative food inflation, and now rising energy prices, we see little prospect of a meaningful reversal in the value-oriented share shift over the next 12-18 months," she said in a report.
  • Investors will want to know the status of the integration of recent acquisition The Reject Shop in Australia. Throughout the year, Nattel expects to see increasingly more evidence of how the transformation is progressing. Nattel says that "as F27 unfolds we expect to see more pronounced impact from merchandise changeover to lower-priced items as pace of SKU transition accelerates."

-Dollarama has been expanding its Latin American footprint. For the quarter, Nattel sees continued positive trends. "Dollarcity contribution expected to remain robust with LatAm seeing similar positive trends to Canada," she says, calling this stream a long-term growth runway for the company.

Write to Adriano Marchese at adriano.marchese@wsj.com

data.title: Enbridge upgraded at BMO on recent pullback, improving growth visibility
data.description:
Enbridge gains 0.6% in Tuesday's trading as BMO Capital upgraded the pipeline operator to Outperform from Market Perform with a C$79.50 price target, saying the stock's recent pullback and improving visibility on growth make an attractive investment in a choppy macroeconomic environment.

Enbridge shares have underperformed Canadian midstream and pipeline peers YTD, likely due to rising bond yields, lack of visibility on the company's ~5% growth guidance through the end of the decade, and a recent equity offering, while peers sport higher perceived growth rates, BMO's Ben Pham said.

The analyst said Enbridge operates more like a diversified utility, prioritizing premium long-duration contracted assets over higher beta abnormal growth, and believes the company's scale, limited commodity exposure, and diversified assets are underappreciated.

"Few companies can boast a visible premium organic growth program like Enbridge, with its $41B in the secured backlog and $20B of new projects expected to be sanctioned in 2026-27," Pham wrote, while opportunistic acquisitions such as Salt Creek Midstream and the Tallgrass crude transport business come with embedded future upside.

Enbridge's ~$3B equity offering and innovative $2.7B joint venture with KKR on its Westcoast B.C. pipeline have shored up the balance sheet, providing additional financial flexibility to fund new growth opportunities that could arise, the analyst said.

data.title: U.S. Treasury Auctions 20-Year Bonds at Highest Yield Since 1986
data.description:
By Paulo Trevisani

The U.S. Treasury on Tuesday auctioned $13 billion in 20-year bonds, with investors demanding the highest yield in four decades.

The bonds sold at a yield of 5.42%, the highest since January 1986, when it was at 9.45%. The 20-year was discontinued later that year before its reintroduction in 2020--and since that point, the highest yield until now had been 5.25% in October 2023.

Despite the elevated payout, demand indicators were on the soft side: the 2.57 bid-to-cover ratio was below the previous six-month average of 2.65, while the share acquired by the indirect-bidders group, which includes foreign investors, was also below trend, at 52.5%.

The tender results come as Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent is trying to cool down long-term yields by buying back more of the government's own debt. Earlier on Tuesday, he said in testimony before the House of Representatives that Treasury auctions have been the "most successful" in 20 years.

The 20-year yield rose to 5.418%, from 5.401% before the auction. Other maturities moved in tandem, with the 10-year rising to 5.014% from 4.996%.

data.title: Creative Planning to Buy Institutional Consultant That Advises on $4.3 Trillion — Barrons.com
data.description:
By Andrew Welsch

Creative Planning is already one of the nation's largest registered investment advisors serving individual investors. Now, it has ambitions to serve more institutional clients too.

To reach that goal, Creative Planning said Tuesday that it has agreed to acquire RVK, an institutional investment consulting firm that advises more than 200 institutional clients with approximately $4.3 trillion in assets. RVK's customers include public and private retirement plans, endowments, foundations, insurance companies, health systems, and other sophisticated asset owners, Creative Planning said. The company didn't disclose terms of the transaction, which it expects to close in January. The deal is subject to regulatory approvals.

"RVK has built an exceptional reputation by providing thoughtful, objective advice to some of the country's most complex institutional investors," says Peter Mallouk, president and CEO of Creative Planning. "Its deep consulting expertise, rigorous investment research, and commitment to putting clients first align closely with how we operate at Creative Planning. Together, we'll be able to bring even greater scale, resources and insight to institutions navigating increasingly complex investment and governance decisions."

Creative Planning managed $419 billion in client assets as of the end of June, according to data the firm submitted to Barron's. The Overland Park, Kan-based company has grown rapidly through acquisitions of dozens of smaller wealth management firms in the U.S. and overseas. It is ranked the No. 2 Mega RIA on Barron's Top 100 RIA Firms for 2026.

RVK is an employee-owned company based in Portland, Ore., and has regional offices in Boise, Idaho; Chicago; and New York, according to its website. RVK provides nondiscretionary investment consulting, helping clients with tasks such as asset allocation, asset studies, investment manager research and selection, and governance consulting. Creative Planning says RVK will continue to be led by its current management team.

"Becoming a Creative Planning affiliate will allow us to preserve the client-focused approach and consulting model that have defined RVK while providing our clients and employees with access to broader resources, technology and capabilities," Josh Kevan, CEO of RVK, says. "We're excited about what our firms can accomplish together."

Goldman Sachs is acting as an exclusive financial advisor to Creative Planning with regard to the transaction, Creative Planning said.

Write to Andrew Welsch at andrew.welsch@barrons.com
